Today's drop in gold prices was highly unusual.

Gold prices fell -3.4% today, marking one of the rarest single-day declines of the last two decades.

Since 2006, gold has recorded an average daily change of +0.05%, with a standard deviation of 1.19%.

Today’s selloff registered a Z-score of -2.90, placing it deep in the left tail of the distribution.

Statistically, a daily decline this extreme occurs just ~0.2% of the time, or roughly once every 2 years assuming a normal distribution.

The surge in yields is creating an extraordinary disruption across the precious metals market.

Credit card stress is hitting young Americans hardest:

Transitions into serious credit card delinquencies for Americans aged 18-29 rose +0.4 percentage points in Q2 2026, to 10.1%, their highest since Q1 2025.

This marks the 2nd consecutive increase, bringing the rate closer to its highest level since Q4 2010.

Serious delinquencies among this age group have more than doubled since Q2 2021.

Furthermore, transitions into 90+ days delinquent credit card debt among Americans aged 70+ rose +0.3 percentage points in Q2, to 6.3%, their highest since Q3 2011.

At the same time, serious delinquencies among those aged 50-59 rose +0.1 percentage points, to 6.4%, their highest level since Q4 2024.

Credit card stress is spreading across multiple generations.

World Labs' Dr. Fei-Fei Li on why the 3D world and spatial intelligence are fundamentally different from language models:

"Language is fundamentally a purely generated signal. There's no language out there. You don't go out in the nature and there's words written in the sky for you."

"Whatever data you feed in, you pretty much can just somehow regurgitate with enough generalizability the same data out, and that's language to language."

"But the 3D world is not. There is a 3D world out there that follows laws of physics, that has its own structures due to materials and many other things. And to fundamentally back that information out and be able to represent it and be able to generate it is just fundamentally quite a different problem."

"We will be borrowing similar ideas or useful ideas from language and LLMs, but this is fundamentally philosophically, to me, a different problem."

@drfeifei

This is an attempt at fixing a serious problem. So many schools charge absurd tuition for degrees that are borderline worthless. The US tax base should not be subsidizing every single degree under the sun. If your 4 year college program is producing graduates that earn less than the *median* salary of someone without a college degree — that’s a terrible look. 

Is this the best solution? What’s the best solution to this problem? I have no idea but subsidizing virtually all college tuition has lead to absurd price inflation and it’s a genuine problem. We address some of this in our book “Both Sides of The Coin”. Here’s a look at college tuition inflation (and other categories) over the last ~30 years.
